                  <jats:p>
                    We consider the primitive decomposition of

                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    , Bott–Chern and Aeppli-harmonic (
                    <jats:italic>k</jats:italic>

                    <jats:inline-formula>

                        <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">

                            <mml:mo>)</mml:mo>
                          </mml:mrow>
                        </mml:math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    . For any
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:tex-math>$$D \in \{\overline{\partial }, \partial , \textrm{BC}, \textrm{A}\}$$</jats:tex-math>
                        <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">

                            </mml:mover>

                          </mml:mrow>
                        </mml:math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>

                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:tex-math>$$L^k P^{0,0}$$</jats:tex-math>
                        <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                          <mml:mrow>

                              </mml:mrow>
                            </mml:msup>
                          </mml:mrow>
                        </mml:math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    component of "Equation missing"
                    
                    is a constant multiple of
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:tex-math>$$\omega ^k$$</jats:tex-math>
                        <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">

                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    up to real dimension 6. In this paper we generalise this result to every dimension. We also deduce information on the components
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:tex-math>$$L^{k-1} P^{1,1}$$</jats:tex-math>
                        <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
        <jats:p>Note: Please see pdf for full abstract with equations.
We consider the primitive decomposition of <jats:italic>∂,∂</jats:italic>, Bott-Chern and Aeppli-harmonic (<jats:italic>k, k</jats:italic>)-forms on compact almost Kähler manifolds (<jats:italic>M, J,ω</jats:italic>). For any <jats:italic>D ∈ {∂, ∂,BC,A}</jats:italic>, it is known that the <jats:italic>L</jats:italic><jats:sup><jats:italic>k</jats:italic></jats:sup><jats:italic>P</jats:italic><jats:sup><jats:italic>0,0</jats:italic></jats:sup> component of <jats:italic>ψ ∈ H</jats:italic><jats:sub><jats:italic>D</jats:italic></jats:sub><jats:sup><jats:italic>k,k</jats:italic></jats:sup> is a constant multiple of <jats:italic>ω</jats:italic><jats:sup><jats:italic>k</jats:italic></jats:sup> up to real dimension 6. In this paper we generalise this result to every dimension. We also deduce information on the components <jats:italic>L</jats:italic><jats:sup><jats:italic>k−1</jats:italic></jats:sup><jats:italic>P</jats:italic><jats:sup><jats:italic>1,1</jats:italic></jats:sup> and <jats:italic>L</jats:italic><jats:sup><jats:italic>k−2</jats:italic></jats:sup><jats:italic>P</jats:italic><jats:sup><jats:italic>2,2</jats:italic></jats:sup> of the primitive decomposion. Focusing on dimension 8, we give a full description of the spaces <jats:italic>H</jats:italic><jats:sub><jats:italic>BC</jats:italic></jats:sub><jats:sup><jats:italic>2,2</jats:italic></jats:sup> and <jats:italic>H</jats:italic><jats:sub><jats:italic>A</jats:italic></jats:sub><jats:sup><jats:italic>2,2</jats:italic></jats:sup>, from which follows <jats:italic>H</jats:italic><jats:sub><jats:italic>BC</jats:italic></jats:sub><jats:sup><jats:italic>2,2</jats:italic></jats:sup><jats:italic> ⊆ H</jats:italic><jats:sub><jats:italic>∂</jats:italic></jats:sub><jats:sup><jats:italic>2,2</jats:italic></jats:sup> and <jats:italic>H</jats:italic><jats:sub><jats:italic>A</jats:italic></jats:sub><jats:sup><jats:italic>2,2</jats:italic></jats:sup><jats:italic> ⊆ H</jats:italic><jats:sub><jats:italic>∂</jats:italic></jats:sub><jats:sup><jats:italic>2,2</jats:italic></jats:sup>. We also provide an almost Kähler 8-dimensional example where the previous inclusions are strict and the primitive components of an harmonic form <jats:italic>ψ ∈ H</jats:italic><jats:sub><jats:italic>D</jats:italic></jats:sub><jats:sup><jats:italic>k,k</jats:italic></jats:sup> are not <jats:italic>D</jats:italic>-harmonic, showing that the primitive decomposition of (<jats:italic>k, k</jats:italic>)-forms in general does not descend to harmonic forms.</jats:p>
title: Primitive Decomposition of Bott-Chern and Dolbeault Harmonic (k,k)-Forms on Compact almost Kähler Manifolds

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
               <jats:p>In this article, we introduce certain arity-3 operations on complex manifolds arising from homotopy transfer theory. Such operations are related to the triple <jats:inline-formula>
                     <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xlink:href="graphic/j_coma-2025-0012_eq_001.png"/>
                        <m:math xmlns:m="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                           <m:mi>A</m:mi>
                           <m:mi>B</m:mi>
                           <m:mi>C</m:mi>
                        </m:math>
                        <jats:tex-math>ABC</jats:tex-math>
                     </jats:alternatives>
                  </jats:inline-formula>-Massey products from Bott-Chern to Aeppli cohomology. We present a package for computing such products as well as other cohomological and homotopical invariants for complex nilmanifolds and give some examples.</jats:p>
title: A ∞-structures for Bott-Chern and Aeppli cohomologies

items.abstract: <jats:p>Degree-weighted alternating sums arise naturally in holomorphic analytic torsion and in Quillen&apos;s determinant line formalism through the action of the number operator. We isolate a simple characteristic form, the weighted Chern character ch𝒩 , defined as the ordinary Chern character of a rational virtual K-theory class ∑q (−1)q · (q/2) · [S(0,q)] attached to a ℤ-graded holomorphic bundle S = ⊕q S(0,q). This viewpoint yields clean functoriality and a Bott–Chern transgression formula by linearity from the classical Bott–Chern theory. A subtlety for torsion is that Dolbeault degrees Ω(0,q) are not holomorphic bundles. We establish precise conjugation sign rules (Lemma 6.1): the degree-2p  Chern–Weil forms of Ω(0,q) and Ω(q,0) are related by the sign (−1)p, while the corresponding Bott–Chern forms are related by the sign (−1)(p−1). We therefore define chDol𝒩  directly using the holomorphic bundles Ω(q,0) with their Chern connections induced by a Hermitian metric. We derive universal low-degree formulas in terms of  ci(TX), compute explicit expressions on Hirzebruch surfaces, and state a threefold top-degree identity applied to Fl(3) and ℙ3. We also position ch𝒩 in the analytic torsion literature as a canonical packaging of the ubiquitous degree-weighted sums produced by the number operator. A λy-reformulation identifies chDol𝒩(X) as the ½(y d/dy)|y = −1 derivative of the Dolbeault generating class ch(λy(Ω(1,0))), making the holomorphic/anti-holomorphic comparison transparent at the level of generating functions. This yields universal reusable identities and drastically reduces sign and combinatorial errors.</jats:p>
title: The Weighted Chern Character chN: A Degree-Weighted Package for Alternating Sums, Bott–Chern Transgression, and Dolbeault Torsion Expressions

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    In this paper, we present explicit computations of non-trivial triple
                    <jats:italic>ABC</jats:italic>
                    –Massey products on non-Kähler solvmanifolds endowed with an invariant complex structure. We prove that the
                    <jats:italic>Bigalke-Rollenske manifold</jats:italic>
                    , the
                    <jats:italic>generalized Nakamura manifolds</jats:italic>
                    satisfying some suitable assumptions and compact quotients of the solvable Lie group
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:tex-math>$$\mathbb {C}^{2n}\ltimes _{\rho } \mathbb {C}^{2m}$$</jats:tex-math>
                        <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                          <mml:mrow>
                            <mml:msup>
                              <mml:mrow>
                                <mml:mi>C</mml:mi>
                              </mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mrow>
                                <mml:mn>2</mml:mn>
                                <mml:mi>n</mml:mi>
                              </mml:mrow>
                            </mml:msup>
                            <mml:msub>
                              <mml:mo>⋉</mml:mo>
                              <mml:mi>ρ</mml:mi>
                            </mml:msub>
                            <mml:msup>
                              <mml:mrow>
                                <mml:mi>C</mml:mi>
                              </mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mrow>
                                <mml:mn>2</mml:mn>
                                <mml:mi>m</mml:mi>
                              </mml:mrow>
                            </mml:msup>
                          </mml:mrow>
                        </mml:math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    have non-vanishing triple
                    <jats:italic>ABC</jats:italic>
                    -Massey products. Furthermore, such manifolds have no astheno-Kähler metric.
                  </jats:p>
title: Aeppli-Bott-Chern Massey products on non-Kähler solvmanifolds
